mainTopic: Offerings on public and private altars in the times of the מדבר, גלגל and שילה, and the rules of the משכן in שילה.
overview: The גמרא first defends רבי יהודה, who allows an individual to bring חובות on a בָּמָה גְּדוֹלָה. It explains that the word אִישׁ teaches that any person, even a זָר who is not a בכור, may serve on a private במה. Next, רב פפא shows that the תנא קמא and the חכמים differ over whether נסכים were brought in the מדבר. רבי שמעון learns from the פסח in גלגל that only fixed-time חובות were brought there, while the חכמים use that פסוק to teach that an ערל may receive הזאה. רב אדא בר אהבה explains a ברייתא about fixed-time offerings as referring to an individual's obligatory עולה, since in his view no מנחה is brought on any במה. The גמרא then turns to שילה, which had stone walls below and curtains above. It also asks how we know that lighter offerings could be eaten anywhere that overlooks שילה. רבי אושעיא and רבי ינאי give one source, and רבי אבדימי בר חסא begins a second one, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יהודה limits the verse to private altars
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה explains that 'the fitting in his eyes' refers only to a private במה. On a בָּמָה גְּדוֹלָה, even חובות may be brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה would answer: the words 'whatever is fitting' are tied to 'in his own eyes,' meaning a private altar. But on the big public altar, even required offerings may be brought.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יהודה against the פסוק that seemed to limit individuals to voluntary offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limit to voluntary offerings is read as tied to the words 'in his own eyes,' which describe a private במה. This leaves the בָּמָה גְּדוֹלָה open for חובות, which is רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: what is fitting in his own eyes
the great public altar
required offerings
may be sacrificed

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda would say to you:
When "whatever is fitting" is written,
it is written about "in his own eyes";
phrases.notes: He means a place the person chooses himself, which is a private altar.

phrases.english: but on a great public altar,
even required offerings may also be sacrificed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers an earlier challenge against רבי יהודה from the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק limits individuals to voluntary offerings everywhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: The limit applies only to a private במה.

steps.title: Doesn't the word 'man' still limit an individual?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says אִישׁ. That seems to teach that an individual may bring only voluntary offerings, never חובות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the verse says 'man.' Doesn't that mean a person may bring only what he chooses, and not required offerings?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה again, this time from the word אִישׁ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if 'in his eyes' refers to a private במה, the word אִישׁ seems to describe any individual. That would block חובות for an individual even on the בָּמָה גְּדוֹלָה.

keyTerms.meaning: a man; an individual
offerings one sees as fitting (voluntary ones)
isn't this to say

phrases.english: But isn't "man" written?
Isn't that to say that a man
may sacrifice only what is fitting,
but required offerings he may not sacrifice?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 1's answer from another word in the same פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view that an individual may bring חובות on a בָּמָה גְּדוֹלָה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word אִישׁ seems to limit any individual to voluntary offerings.

steps.title: 'Man' teaches that a non-priest may serve
steps.stepSummary: The word אִישׁ does not limit which offerings may be brought. It teaches that a זָר may serve on a private במה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When 'man' is written, it comes to allow a non-כהן to do the service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the word אִישׁ a different job, so it no longer works against רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אִישׁ is understood as 'any man,' meaning anyone, not just a כהן, may serve on a private במה. Since the word is used for this lesson, it says nothing about which offerings are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: to make valid; to permit
a non-כהן

phrases.english: When "man" is written,
it is to permit a non-priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 2 by giving the word another purpose.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אִישׁ limits an individual to voluntary offerings.
steps.terutzMaskana: אִישׁ teaches that a זָר may serve on a private במה.

steps.title: The non-priest rule is already known from another verse
steps.stepSummary: The rule that a זָר may serve on a private במה is already learned from 'the כהן shall dash the blood on the altar of ה׳.' So why is אִישׁ needed for it?
steps.simpleTranslation: A non-priest? That is already learned from 'And the priest shall dash the blood on the altar of ה׳'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that the lesson given to אִישׁ is not needed, since another פסוק already teaches it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That פסוק requires a כהן only at the altar of the אהל מועד. This implies that on a private במה, a זָר may serve. If so, the word אִישׁ would be extra, and it could go back to limiting offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: and he shall dash (the blood)
it is derived

phrases.english: A non-priest? From "And the priest shall dash

phrases.aramaic: אֶת הַדָּם עַל מִזְבַּח ה׳״ נָפְקָא!
phrases.english: the blood against the altar of the Lord" it is derived!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:6

steps.triggerLanguage: זָר – מִ״וְּזָרַק הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הַדָּם עַל מִזְבַּח ה׳״ נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 3's answer as not needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using אִישׁ to permit a זָר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The lesson is already known from ויקרא 17:6, so אִישׁ would be extra.

steps.title: 'Man' teaches that firstborn status is not needed
steps.stepSummary: Without אִישׁ, one might think the non-כהן serving on a במה must be a בכור, as it was before the משכן. אִישׁ teaches that any man may serve.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought it requires the holiness of the firstborn, as at the start. So the verse teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that אִישׁ adds a new point beyond the other פסוק, so it is not extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other פסוק shows only that a כהן is not required. One could still think only בכורות may serve, since they did the service before the משכן. אִישׁ teaches that any person may bring his own offering on a private במה.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have said
the holiness of the firstborn
as at first (before the משכן)
it teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, 'whatever is fitting in his eyes' applies only to a private במה. The word אִישׁ teaches that any person, not only a כהן or a בכור, may serve there.

phrases.english: You might have said it requires
the holiness of the firstborn, as at first;
phrases.notes: Before the משכן was built, the firstborn did the service.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא לִיבְעֵי קִדּוּשׁ בְּכוֹרוֹת כְּמֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by showing that אִישׁ teaches something new.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: the word blocks a mistaken assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only בכורות may serve on a private במה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any man may serve on a private במה.

steps.title: The Sages seem to repeat the first opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the view of the חכמים in the ברייתא looks identical to the view of the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The view of the Sages is the same as the first opinion!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that two opinions in the ברייתא seem to say the same thing. It asks what the difference between them is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא would not quote two opinions that say the exact same thing. Both the תנא קמא and the חכמים seem to say that an individual on a private במה brought only עולות and שלמים. So there must be some hidden difference, and the גמרא wants to find it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages; here, the group quoted at the end of the ברייתא
That is the same as
The first teacher; the opening opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: The Sages, that is the same as the first teacher!
phrases.notes: The 'first teacher' is the opinion quoted at the very start of the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the discussion of רבי יהודה's view to a new question about two other opinions in the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's choice to quote the חכמים as a separate opinion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two opinions with the same content would be pointless repetition, so the separate quote needs to be explained.

steps.title: They disagree about libations in the wilderness
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the two opinions differ on whether נסכים were brought in the מדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The difference between them is whether libations were offered in the wilderness.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. He shows that the two opinions really do disagree, about נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree about which animal offerings were brought, but they disagree about the נסכים that go along with them. According to the תנא קמא, נסכים were not brought in the מדבר. According to the חכמים, they were. So the repetition is not pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Libations; wine poured on the מזבח together with certain offerings
The wilderness, where בני ישראל traveled before entering ארץ ישראל
The difference between them is

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Whether libations were offered in the wilderness is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: קָרְבוּ נְסָכִים בְּמִדְבָּר אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by finding a real difference between the two opinions.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a practical difference between seemingly identical opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים and the תנא קמא say exactly the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ over whether נסכים were offered in the מדבר.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's opinion from the ברייתא and asks for his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי שמעון says, and so on. What is רבי שמעון's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another opinion in the ברייתא, that of רבי שמעון. It asks what his source is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that even the public did not bring every kind of offering in גלגל. They brought only the פסח and חובות that have a set time. The גמרא wants to know what in the פסוקים tells him this.

keyTerms.meaning: What is his reason?

phrases.english: The Master said:
Rabbi Shimon says, and so on.
phrases.notes: 'And so on' points to the rest of his words in the ברייתא: in גלגל only the פסח and fixed-time חובות were brought.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר וְכוּ׳. מַאי טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תנא קמא and חכמים question and opens a new topic about רבי שמעון.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for רבי שמעון's limit on offerings in גלגל

steps.title: The verse about the Passover in גלגל
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק saying that בני ישראל brought the פסח in גלגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And the children of Israel kept the Passover in גלגל."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי שמעון's source: a פסוק in יהושע about bringing the פסח in גלגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions only the פסח when it describes the offerings in גלגל. רבי שמעון reads this as a hint about what kind of offerings were allowed there. The next steps explain exactly how.

keyTerms.meaning: The Passover offering, brought on the fourteenth of ניסן
The first camp of בני ישראל in ארץ ישראל, where the משכן stood

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And the children of Israel made"
phrases.notes: יהושע 5:10

phrases.english: "the Passover offering in Gilgal."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וַיַּעֲשׂוּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הַפֶּסַח בַּגִּלְגָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק that describes bringing the פסח in גלגל

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that of course they brought the פסח, so the פסוק seems to teach nothing new.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof. It says that bringing the פסח is obvious, so how does this פסוק show anything?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסח is a required offering, and nobody would think it was not brought in גלגל. A פסוק that only tells us something obvious seems to have no lesson for רבי שמעון to learn from it. The גמרא now needs to find a hidden lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; used to challenge a statement that seems to add nothing

phrases.english: It is obvious!
phrases.notes: Of course they brought the פסח; it is a required offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the usefulness of the פסוק quoted in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק about the פסח in גלגל as a source for רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק stating something obvious cannot be the basis for a new limitation.

steps.title: Only offerings like the Passover were brought
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק teaches that in גלגל only חובות similar to the פסח, ones with a set time, were brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it teaches us this: required offerings that are like the Passover were brought, but those that are not like the Passover were not brought.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own challenge. The פסוק is not telling us that the פסח was brought. It is telling us that only offerings like the פסח were brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because bringing the פסח is obvious, mentioning it must have a purpose: to set it as the model. Offerings similar to the פסח, meaning public חובות with a fixed time, were brought in גלגל. Offerings unlike the פסח were not. This is exactly רבי שמעון's view.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
Required offerings
Similar to the פסח; here, having a set time

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, in גלגל the public brought only the פסח and חובות like it, which have a set time. He learns this because the פסוק mentions the obvious פסח, so it must be teaching a limit.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק does not mean that ONLY the פסח itself was brought. It means offerings that are LIKE the פסח, fixed-time חובות, were brought.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it teaches us:
that required offerings similar to the Passover offering are what was offered,
phrases.notes: 'Similar to the פסח' means offerings that have a set time, like the פסח does.

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָאו כְּעֵין פֶּסַח לָא קָרֵב.
phrases.english: but those not similar to the Passover offering were not offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 10 by finding a hidden limit in the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets an obvious statement as setting a model or category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק only says the פסח was brought, which is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק makes the פסח a model: only fixed-time חובות like it were brought in גלגל.

steps.title: How does the other opinion read the verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to ask how the חכמים, who disagree with רבי שמעון, explain this פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to ask how the opinion that disagrees with רבי שמעון explains the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים hold that in גלגל the public brought other offerings too, not only ones like the פסח. So they must read the פסוק differently. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one; refers to the opinion that disagrees

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: 'The other one' is the חכמים who disagree with רבי שמעון. How do they explain the פסוק?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining רבי שמעון's reading, turns to ask how the other side handles the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the חכמים, who disagree with רבי שמעון, understand the פסוק about the פסח in גלגל

steps.title: The Sages use the verse for רבי יוחנן's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים do not learn רבי שמעון's rule from the פסוק about the פסח in גלגל. They need it for רבי יוחנן's teaching that an ערל may receive הזאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need the verse for the teaching of רבי יוחנן, who said in the name of רבי בנאה: an uncircumcised man may receive the sprinkling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from the last step. The חכמים use this פסוק for a different lesson: an uncircumcised person can be sprinkled with the purifying water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון learned from the פסוק that only fixed-time offerings like the פסח were brought in גלגל. The חכמים use the same פסוק for something else. In יהושע's time the people were purified with the sprinkling before they were circumcised, which shows that an ערל may receive הזאה.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (the פסוק) for a different teaching
An uncircumcised man
Sprinkling of the red heifer water to purify from corpse impurity

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides use the same פסוק. רבי שמעון learns from it what was offered in גלגל, while the חכמים learn from it that an ערל may receive הזאה.

phrases.english: They need it for the teaching of Rabbi Yochanan,
phrases.notes: "It" is the פסוק about the פסח in גלגל from the earlier steps.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי בַּנָּאָה:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Bena'a:
An uncircumcised man may receive sprinkling.
phrases.notes: This is the sprinkling of red heifer water, which purifies someone from corpse impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 about how the חכמים explain the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים use the פסוק to teach that an ערל may receive הזאה.

steps.title: A teaching on the difference between public and private altars
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites a ברייתא before רב אדא בר אהבה. It says the only difference between a במה גדולה and a במה קטנה is the פסח and fixed-time obligatory offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רב אדא בר אהבה: The only difference between a great altar and a small altar is the פסח and obligatory offerings that have a set time.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section starts. Someone recites a ברייתא listing what may be brought only on the public altar, and this sets up רב אדא בר אהבה's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא matches רבי שמעון's view from earlier. Only the פסח and fixed-time obligatory offerings needed the public altar. Everything else could also be brought on a private one.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, a person whose job was to memorize and recite ברייתות
A great (public) altar, like the one in גלגל
A small (private) altar that an individual builds
Obligatory offerings that have a fixed time

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rav Adda bar Ahava:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּין בָּמָה גְּדוֹלָה לְבָמָה קְטַנָּה,
phrases.english: There is no difference between a great altar and a small altar,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא פֶּסַח וְחוֹבוֹת הַקָּבוּעַ לָהֶן זְמַן.
phrases.english: except the Paschal offering and obligatory offerings that have a set time.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion that connects to רבי שמעון's rule about fixed-time offerings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the פסח and fixed-time obligatory offerings are limited to the במה גדולה.

steps.title: An individual has no fixed-time obligatory offerings
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה objects that a private person never has fixed-time obligatory offerings. So why mention them in a list about private altars?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: An individual, where would he have obligatory offerings with a set time?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא challenges the wording of the ברייתא. A private altar is used by individuals, and individuals don't have fixed-time obligatory offerings, so mentioning them seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fixed-time obligatory offerings are usually brought by the community, like the daily and holiday offerings. Since an individual would never bring such an offering on his private altar, there seems to be no reason to say it is not allowed there.

keyTerms.meaning: An individual, a private person
From where would he have it?

phrases.english: He said to him: An individual —

phrases.aramaic: חוֹבוֹת שֶׁקָּבוּעַ לָהֶן זְמַן מְנָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: where would he have obligatory offerings that have a set time?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יָחִיד חוֹבוֹת שֶׁקָּבוּעַ לָהֶן זְמַן מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase "fixed-time obligatory offerings" in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A private altar serves individuals, and individuals have no fixed-time obligatory offerings, so the phrase adds nothing.

steps.title: Should the words be removed?
steps.stepSummary: The תנא asks whether he should take those words out of the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Should I remove it?
steps.whatsHappening: The תנא responds to the challenge by asking if he should simply erase the phrase. This sets up רב אדא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the phrase really has no meaning, the simple fix would be to teach only "the פסח." The תנא asks whether that is the correct move.

keyTerms.meaning: Should I remove it (from the text)?

phrases.english: He said to him: Should I remove it?
phrases.notes: He's asking: should I erase the words about fixed-time offerings from the ברייתא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The תנא reacts to step 15's objection by offering to remove the words.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the phrase should be taken out of the ברייתא.

steps.title: Explain it as an individual's obligatory burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא says not to remove it. Read the ברייתא as talking about an obligatory עולה, as opposed to a voluntary one. It cannot mean a חטאת, since an individual has no fixed-time חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Explain your teaching as dealing with an obligatory burnt offering, since there is also a voluntary burnt offering. For if it meant an individual's sin offering, are there obligatory ones with a set time?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא saves the wording. He shows there is one individual offering that fits: an obligatory עולה that has a set time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An individual does have an obligatory עולה with a fixed time, such as the עולת ראייה brought on the רגלים. That one needs the public altar, while a voluntary עולה can go on a private altar. The case cannot be a חטאת, because an individual's חטאת comes from a sin and has no set time.

keyTerms.meaning: Explain it as / interpret it as
An obligatory burnt offering
A voluntary burnt offering
An individual's sin offering

phrases.english: He said to him: Explain your teaching
phrases.notes: "Your teaching" is the ברייתא the תנא just recited, not the משנה.

phrases.english: as dealing with an obligatory burnt offering,
since there is also a voluntary burnt offering.
For if it is an individual's sin offering —

phrases.aramaic: חוֹבוֹת דִּקְבִיעַ לֵיהּ זְמַן מִי אִיכָּא?!
phrases.english: are there obligatory ones with a set time?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תִּתַּרְגַּם מַתְנִיתָךְ בְּעוֹלַת חוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 15 and turns down step 16's suggestion to remove the words.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the ברייתא refers to a specific individual offering.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Individuals have no fixed-time obligatory offerings, so the phrase is useless.
steps.terutzMaskana: An individual's obligatory עולה has a set time. It is limited to the public altar, unlike a voluntary עולה.

steps.title: Why not use the obligatory meal offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב אדא did not explain the ברייתא as the מנחת חביתין, an obligatory meal offering with a set time.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him explain it as an obligatory meal offering, since there is the griddle-cake offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אדא's choice of example. There seems to be an easier fixed-time offering he could have used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חביתין is brought by one person, the כהן גדול, every day at a set time. It seems like an obvious example of an individual's fixed-time obligation, so why didn't רב אדא mention it?

keyTerms.meaning: Let him explain it as (set it in a different case)
An obligatory meal offering
The daily griddle-cake meal offering of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: But let him explain it as an obligatory meal offering —
since there is the griddle-cake offering!
phrases.notes: This is the meal offering the כהן גדול brings every day, half in the morning and half in the evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלוֹקְמַהּ בְּמִנְחַת חוֹבָה דְּהָא אִיכָּא חֲבִיתִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the example רב אדא chose in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא's choice of the obligatory עולה as the example.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חביתין is an individual's fixed-time obligation too, and seems an even more natural example.

steps.title: No meal offering on an outside altar
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא holds that no מנחה is brought on any במה, so the חביתין could not be the case in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: there is no meal offering on a במה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that, in רב אדא's view, meal offerings were never brought on any במה at all. So they can't be the difference between the two kinds of altars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists things allowed on the public altar but not the private one. If no מנחה is brought on any במה, even a public one, then the חביתין doesn't fit that list. That leaves the obligatory עולה as the correct example.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this is his opinion)
No meal offering is brought on an altar outside the Temple

steps.whatToRemember: רב אדא בר אהבה explains the ברייתא as the individual's obligatory עולה. A מנחה doesn't work, because in his view no מנחה is offered on any במה.
steps.confusionAlert: "No מנחה on a במה" includes even the public במה גדולה, not only private altars. That is why the חביתין can't show a difference between them.

phrases.english: He holds: there is no meal offering on a במה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to the speaker's own legal position.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חביתין could serve as the individual's fixed-time offering on the public altar.
steps.terutzMaskana: No מנחה is brought on any במה, so only the obligatory עולה fits the ברייתא.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the שילה rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about arriving at שילה and asks where its description comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said, 'They came to שילה, etc.' Where do we learn these things from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה, about the משכן in שילה, and asks for its source. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the משכן in שילה had no roof, only stone walls below and curtains above. The גמרא wants a פסוק that shows this.

keyTerms.meaning: The town where the משכן stood for many years, after the time of גלגל
From where do we know these things? (a request for a source)
Etc.; the quote from the משנה continues

phrases.english: The משנה said: 'They came to Shiloh, etc.'
phrases.notes: This is the part of the משנה that says there was no roof in שילה, just stone below and curtains above.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic in the משנה after the discussion of fixed-time offerings on a במה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק that shows the משכן in שילה was stone walls with curtains above.

steps.title: Verses calling שילה both a house and a tent
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings one פסוק that calls the place in שילה a 'house' and others that call it a 'tent'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: One פסוק says, 'And she brought him to the house of ה׳ in שילה.' Another פסוק says, 'He forsook the Tabernacle of שילה, the tent He had placed among men.' And it is written, 'He rejected the tent of יוסף, and did not choose the tribe of אפרים.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers by bringing פסוקים that seem to describe שילה in two different ways. One calls it a house and others call it a tent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A house is a solid building, while a tent is made of cloth. So the פסוקים seem to disagree about what stood in שילה. The next step shows how both are true.

keyTerms.meaning: The house of ה׳, which sounds like a solid building
A tent, which sounds like a cloth structure
The Tabernacle
One פסוק says... (the opening of two פסוקים set against each other)

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
One verse says:
'And she brought him to the house of the Lord in Shiloh,'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 1:24. This is חנה bringing שמואל to the משכן.

phrases.english: and another verse says:
'And He forsook the Tabernacle of Shiloh,
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the printed גמרא, but the פסוק itself does not have it.

phrases.english: the tent that He had placed among men,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 78:60

phrases.english: and it is also written:
'And He rejected the tent of Joseph,
and He did not choose the tribe of Ephraim.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 78:67. This פסוק also calls the place a 'tent'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of step 20 by laying out two kinds of פסוקים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוקים call שילה both a 'house' and a 'tent'. Putting them together will show what the structure was.

steps.title: Stone walls below, curtains above
steps.stepSummary: The פסוקים fit together: שילה had stone walls (a house) with curtains on top (a tent), and it was called 'rest'.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can both be true? There was no roof there. There were stones below and curtains above. And that place was called 'rest'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the two kinds of פסוקים fit together. The structure was partly a house and partly a tent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stone walls are why it is called a 'house'. The cloth curtains used as a roof are why it is called a 'tent'. This is exactly what the משנה said, so now the משנה has its source.

keyTerms.meaning: How can this be? (how do the sources fit together)
A roof made of wood or stone
The curtains of the משכן
'Rest', the name the תורה uses for the period of שילה

steps.whatToRemember: שילה was both a 'house' and a 'tent': stone walls below and the curtains of the משכן above, with no real roof.

phrases.english: How can this be?
There was no roof there,
but rather stones below,
and curtains above,
and that was the 'rest.'
phrases.notes: This is the word 'rest' in דברים 12:9. The time of שילה is what that פסוק calls 'rest'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the clash between the 'house' and 'tent' פסוקים of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both פסוקים are true, each describing a different part of the building.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that the פסוקים disagree about whether שילה was a house or a tent.
steps.terutzMaskana: It had stone walls below (a house) and curtains above (a tent), just as the משנה says.

steps.title: Asking for the source about eating offerings in שילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה, about קדשי קדשים, and asks for a source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said, 'קדשי קדשים...' Where do we learn these things from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about where offerings were eaten in שילה, and asks for its source. This sets up רבי אושעיא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that in שילה, קדשי קדשים were eaten inside the curtains, but קדשים קלים and מעשר שני could be eaten anywhere you could see שילה from. The real question is where the 'anywhere you can see' rule comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The most holy offerings, eaten only inside the curtains
Offerings of lesser holiness, which in שילה could be eaten anywhere you could see it from
Second tithe, which also had to be eaten near the משכן

phrases.english: The משנה said: 'Offerings of the most sacred order...'
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on to say that the lighter offerings were eaten anywhere you could see שילה from. That is the part being asked about.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the structure of שילה to the rules of eating offerings there.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that קדשים קלים and מעשר שני could be eaten anywhere that overlooks שילה.

steps.title: You may not offer anywhere you see, but you may eat there
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא learns from a פסוק: you may not offer up anywhere you see, but you may eat anywhere you see.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא said: The פסוק says, 'Be careful not to offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see.' This means: in every place you see, you may not offer up, but you may eat in every place you see.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא gives the source. He reads a פסוק as saying that 'every place you see' is not allowed for offering, but is allowed for eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only forbids offering up in 'every place you see'. רבי אושעיא learns from this that eating there is allowed. So in שילה, any place from which you can see it is fine for eating קדשים קלים.

keyTerms.meaning: Offer up, meaning burn an offering on the מזבח
In every place that you see
Eat

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya said:
As the verse says:
'Be careful that you do not offer up your burnt offerings
in every place that you see' —
phrases.notes: דברים 12:13. The word in round brackets is in the printed גמרא, but the פסוק itself does not have it.

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל מָקוֹם אֲשֶׁר תִּרְאֶה אִי אַתָּה מַעֲלֶה,
phrases.english: in every place that you see you may not offer up,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה אוֹכֵל בְּכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה רוֹאֶה.
phrases.english: but you may eat in every place that you see.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'do not offer up in every place you see' we learn that eating in every place you see is allowed.

steps.title: Maybe the verse allows slaughtering, not eating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: maybe the פסוק means you may not offer up anywhere you see, but you may slaughter there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: in every place you see you may not offer up, but you may slaughter in every place you see!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אושעיא's reading. It suggests the פסוק could be allowing slaughtering, not eating, in 'every place you see'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says what is forbidden: offering up. It does not say what is allowed. So why assume it allows eating? Maybe it allows slaughtering the animal there, and then רבי אושעיא's source would not prove the משנה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (a suggestion for a different reading)
Slaughter (an offering)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that slaughtering outside really is allowed. It is only showing that רבי אושעיא's reading is not the only possible one.

phrases.english: Say instead:

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה רוֹאֶה אִי אַתָּה מַעֲלֶה,
phrases.english: in every place that you see you may not offer up,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַתָּה זוֹבֵחַ בְּכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁתִּרְאֶה!
phrases.english: but you may slaughter in every place that you see!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference רבי אושעיא made in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's reading that the פסוק allows eating in 'every place you see'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק only forbids offering up. What it allows could just as well be slaughtering as eating, so the proof is not clear.

steps.title: Slaughtering must also be in the chosen place
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי answers the challenge: 'there you shall offer up, and there you shall do' shows that all the service, including slaughter, stays in the chosen place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: The פסוק says, 'There you shall offer up and there you shall do.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי answers the challenge from step 25. He shows that slaughtering also may not be done 'anywhere you see.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge asked: maybe only offering up is limited to the chosen place, and slaughtering is allowed outside. רבי ינאי points to the next פסוק, which says 'there you shall offer up' and then adds 'and there you shall do.' That covers every act of service, slaughtering included. So the only thing allowed 'anywhere you see' is eating.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall offer up (burn on the מזבח)
You shall do (here: every act of the service)

steps.whyThisMatters: This confirms that in the time of שילה, eating קדשים קלים was allowed anywhere you could see שילה from, but slaughtering was not.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said: The verse states:
"There you shall offer up... and there you shall do."
phrases.notes: דברים 12:14. The dots mean the גמרא skips the words in between and quotes only the two parts it needs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25, that maybe slaughtering is allowed 'anywhere you see.'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings an extra phrase of the פסוק that widens the limit to every act of service.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe only offering up must be in the chosen place, and slaughtering may be done anywhere you see.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'And there you shall do' includes slaughtering, so only eating is allowed anywhere you see.

steps.title: A second source begins
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבדימי בר חסא starts to bring a different פסוק to answer the same question; the quote continues in the next part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבדימי בר חסא said: The פסוק says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second answer, from רבי אבדימי בר חסא. His פסוק is quoted in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another way to explain the law about where to eat and where to slaughter in the time of שילה. Here we only have the opening words. His actual פסוק and how he reads it come right after this.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the proof here yet. This line only opens his statement, and the פסוק comes next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Avdimi bar Ḥasa said,
the verse states:

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי אבדימי בר חסא אמר אמר קרא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a different source for the same law, alongside רבי אושעיא and רבי ינאי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different פסוק (still to be quoted) as the source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think רבי ינאי's reading is the only source.
steps.terutzMaskana: A second source is being offered; its details follow in the next part.
